claims.explanation: Deforolimus is an allosteric mTORC1 inhibitor (rapalog), so sensitivity is expected in tumors whose growth depends on mTORC1-driven translation downstream of activated PI3K/AKT signaling. The most consistent genomic predictors are activating PIK3CA mutations and PTEN loss, which hyperactivate AKT/mTORC1 and are enriched in the selectively killed lines (HCC1954, HGC27, KYSE510, KYSE70, ZR751, BT549, 786O), while RAS/BRAF-driven lines without PI3K-pathway lesions (IPC298, UACC62, most KRAS colorectal/pancreatic lines) are relatively resistant.

features.basis: PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT/mTORC1; enriched in killed lines (ZR751, BT549, 786O)
Activating PI3K mutation drives mTORC1 dependence; seen in HCC1954, HGC27, KYSE510, KYSE70
Higher mTOR pathway activity increases dependence on mTORC1 signaling
AKT overexpression activates mTORC1 and is a reported mTOR-pathway deregulation
S6K1 overexpression marks active mTORC1 output and pathway addiction
4EBP1 overexpression reflects mTORC1-driven translation dependence
eIF4E overexpression is a reported mTOR-pathway alteration in cancers
LKB1 loss activates AMPK-independent mTORC1 but killed lung lines with STK11 mutations are few; weak evidence
KRAS-driven lines (GSU, T3M4, PATU8988S, CL11) are among least affected, suggesting RAS/MAPK bypass of mTORC1 dependence
BRAF-mutant melanoma UACC62 is least affected; MAPK-driven growth less mTORC1-dependent
NF2-mutant mesothelioma NCIH2052 is least affected; weak, lineage-limited evidence
TP53 mutation is near-universal in both extremes, so it is not selective; listed only as a non-predictive control
